changes.summary: While photography gained a foothold as a fine art medium between the 1960s and 1990s, women worked across the full range of contemporary photographic practice and pushed it in new directions. To See and Be Seen presents pictures by nineteen female photographers who examined society, expanded definitions of genre and craft, and explored topics of memory, identity, and the uses and materials of photography—often while working against social and institutional conventions that advantaged men. From large-scale Polaroids to palm-sized postcards, this concise selection of photographs from CAM’s collection lends insight into a transformative period for culture, institutions, and art photography. Featured artists include photographers Eleanor Antin, Diane Arbus, Ruth Bernhard, Ellen Carey, Anita Douthat, Maureen France, Lorna Simpson, Cindy Sherman, and Constance Sullivan.
